draft.title: Functional movement assessment
card: A functional movement assessment tests how well a person moves in everyday and sporting tasks, such as squatting, lunging, reaching or balancing on one leg.
It is done before a person starts a program. It shows movement limits, weak links or imbalances, so the program can be set at a suitable level.
things such as joint range, strength, balance, past injury and body control.
psychological factors include confidence, motivation and fear of injury. Sociocultural factors include cultural beliefs, family duties, cost and access to facilities.
draft.remember: Check how a person moves, and what shapes their movement, before planning their program.

a.q: Why is a functional movement assessment done before a person starts a new training program?
opts: To find movement limits so the program suits the person
To prove the person is ready for the hardest exercises
To rank the person against others in their age group
To replace the need for any later checks of progress
a.why: The assessment shows how the person moves now, including limits and imbalances, so the program can be set at a suitable level. It is not a ranking against others, because it looks at the individual's own movement.
a.clue: Think about what the results help the coach to plan.

b.q: Leila, 16, wants to join a gym in Ballarat. Her assessment shows good squat form. She says she avoids gyms because she fears being judged, and she cannot afford the fees. Which of her factors is psychological?
opts: Her fear of being judged at the gym
Her good squat form in the assessment
Her lack of money to pay gym fees
Her age of 16 years at the time of testing
b.why: Fear of being judged is about her thoughts and feelings, so it is psychological. Cost is a sociocultural factor, since it affects her access to a facility. Squat form is a physical factor.
b.clue: Which one is about her thoughts and feelings, not her body or her money?

a.best: To find movement limits so the program suits the person

b.best: Her fear of being judged at the gym
